description_full: TRX Gold Corporation engages in the exploration, development, and production of mineral property in Tanzania. Its flagship project is the Buckreef Gold Project in Tanzania. The company was formerly known as Tanzanian Gold Corporation and changed its name to TRX Gold Corporation in May 2022. The company was incorporated in 1990 and is based in Oakville, Canada.
ceo_bio: Mr. Stephen  Mullowney B.B.A., C.A., C.F.A., CPA | CEO & Director | Age 48 | Compensation: $953,937 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 336 people. Revenue per employee of $171K ranks in the bottom quartile among Basic Materials peers, with revenue growing 23%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $10K of free cash flow annually. CEO compensation is 6× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: TRX Gold Corporation is a micro-cap basic materials business with a $260M market cap on $58M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -3.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 9% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 44%.

The business throws off $3M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.48× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

sect: Its 25% operating margin runs 16pp above the Basic Materials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.92x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+42.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 222 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 39% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 35% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 72% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 90% and a beta of 0.80, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.27 vs 5y 0.58), so read it loosely.
About $2.0M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 39% in the 2020 crash, 42% in the 2022 bear market and 75% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $0.40 (margin of safety -99%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 2%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $0.11 to $1.34 (P10-P90).
Multiples send mixed signals against Basic Materials peers: cheaper on P/E 7.9 vs 15.4, richer on P/FCF 74.4 vs 21.8 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.3% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $2.36 on average, 198% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 28.7% annual cash-flow growth, 12pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 8.6%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.25).
It runs a 44% gross margin and converts 6% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.48x.
ROE of 11% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $7.8M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.1, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 22.6% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 13.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 33.2% on average.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.6%, and institutions hold 9%.
people: With about 336 employees, each generates about $171K of revenue, 0.3x the Basic Materials median, and revenue has grown 22.6% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $10K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $954K (6x revenue per employee).
